why_how.text: Do not hang items from the mirror or cover the windshield with decals that may obstruct the view.

Check the seat and mirror settings before starting to drive.
Set the seat high enough to see the road clearly, using a cushion if needed.
Do not place the seat so far forward that steering becomes difficult.
Set the interior rearview mirror to show the view through the back window.
Adjust side mirrors to show the sides, with the vehicle side visible when leaning slightly forward.
Set a day-and-night mirror for the lighting conditions in which you will drive.
A head restraint is intended to reduce whiplash in a rear impact.
Adjust the head restraint so that it contacts the back of the head.

why_how.text: Montana makes the driver responsible for ensuring occupants are properly belted or secured in child safety seats, subject to the listed legal exceptions.
Use the safety belt on every trip, including short trips at low speed.
Before leaving, fasten your belt and check that passengers are using belts or child restraints.
Lock the vehicle doors before driving away.
A two-part belt system requires both the lap portion and the shoulder portion for its intended protection.
With an automatic shoulder belt, buckle the lap belt too.
Using only one portion of a lap-and-shoulder system substantially reduces protection.
An unrestrained occupant can strike and seriously injure other people in the vehicle during a crash.
The listed seatbelt-law exceptions include vehicles manufactured before January one, nineteen sixty-eight.
An occupant unable to wear a belt for medical reasons needs to carry a physician’s written statement to use the stated exemption.
The stated special-mobile-equipment seatbelt exemption applies to the operator of a vehicle licensed in that category.
Special mobile equipment is not primarily designed or used to transport people or property and is moved on highways only incidentally.
A driver making frequent stops as part of official job duties may receive a seatbelt exemption from the Department of Justice.
The handbook points frequent-stop workers to exemption form MVD-SE1.
